mutations.label: XA THE SAFETY GATE GOES: stale build checks are re-recorded as success with NO passing api_smoke run behind them. #511 re-records a stale opinion as success on purpose, so this one condition is the whole difference between 'outranks a stale opinion with runtime proof' and 'fabricates success'. verification_checklist_not_ready blocks 66 corpus runs.
mutations.find:
if not passing:
        return 0  # no proof the app built + booted + served → do NOT fabricate success
mutations.replace:
if False:
        return 0  # no proof the app built + booted + served → do NOT fabricate success

mutations.label: XB a run that FAILED after the passing one no longer invalidates it, so a build broken since the proof still reads as success. The pass is evidence about a moment, not a standing fact.
mutations.find: return 0  # a later run broke the build → the earlier pass is stale
mutations.replace: pass      # a later run broke the build → the earlier pass is stale

mutations.label: XC the name filter admits every check, so unrelated checks are re-recorded as success off an api_smoke pass that says nothing about them.

XD the already-success skip goes, so every matching check is rewritten on every pass. #1202bu's shape: re-recording a check that is already success is churn the checklist reader cannot distinguish from a real transition.
XE the deterministic-evidence marker goes, so the re-record no longer OUTRANKS the stale opinion it was written to override (#258). The record lands and changes nothing.
